newsitem.title: USA: GM Chairman Smith 1996 compensation up 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: GM Chairman Smith 1996 compensation up 2 pct.

text.p: General Motors Corp said on Wednesday that the total compensation granted Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and President John Smith Jr in 1996 amounted to $5,660,000, up about two percent from the 1995 level.
Total compensation includes salary, an annual bonus and long-term incentives, according to GM's proxy statement which was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission today.
Smith's base salary of $1,750,000 was up about 16.7 percent compared to 1995, as reported in last year's proxy, in part reflecting his election as chairman of the GM board in January 1996.

His annual incentive of $1,600,000 was down 8.6 percent, and his long-term performance incentive of $2,310,000 was virtually unchanged versus the prior year. Smith also received a grant of 200,000 stock options during 1996.
Harry Pearce, vice chairman received salary and incentives totaling $2,945,000 and stock options for 101,300 GM shares and 31,400 GMH shares.
The base salary for Pearce was increased 11.8 percent compared to the year earlier, partly reflecting his election to the board as vice chairman in January 1996.

GM Executive Vice President Louis Hughes received salary and incentives of $2,905,000 and stock options for 100,000 GM shares. Executive Vice President G. Richard Wagoner Jr received salary and incentives of $2,905,000 and stock options for 100,000 GM shares. Hughes Electronics Chairman and Chief Executive C. Michael Armstrong received salary and incentives of $2,872,000 and options for 105,000 GMH shares.

The base salary for Hughes and Wagoner increased about 8.8 percent compared to 1995. The annual incentive payouts, or bonuses, were down more than six percent for Pearce, and down eight percent for Hughes and Wagoner, compared to 1995.
Long-term incentive payouts for these three executives were five percent higher than 1995 long-term payouts.

Armstrong's base salary increased about 29 percent, and his annual incentive increased 10.3 percent compared to the prior year, in part reflecting his election to the GM President's Council during 1995.

GM's Executive Compensation Committee of the Board oversees compensation decisions for executives. The Committee again established aggressive profitability and other financial targets that had to be achieved for payouts of 1996 annual bonuses, GM said in a statement.
GM's annual shareholder meeting will take place May 23 in Wilmington, Delaware, according to the proxy statement.

Stockholders are being asked to approve three management proposals this year -- approval of an independent auditor, revisions to a long-term stock incentive program for non-employee directors, and a five-year incentive plan for GM executives. The corporation's current executive compensation plan expires in May 1997.

The proxy statement also includes five stockholder proposals which the GM board opposes -- limits for director service, cumulative voting, an independent board chairman, independent directors and stock options for directors.

One proposal, also submitted last year, seeks to separate the positions of chief executive and board chairman, both of which Smith currently holds. Smith was named chairman in January 1996, succeeding John Smale, who remains a director.
